semantic_fragments.content: Clause 8.1: A lay operator in the home healthcare environment can perform the cleaning or cleaning and disinfection processes when intended (see 7.4.7). Usability of each such process pertaining to a lay operator was investigated by the usability engineering process. Result: Usability was evaluated in the Usability test report / See usability engineering file. Verdict: P.

Clause 8.3.1 IP rating determination: The device is not transit-operable, handheld, or body-worn ME equipment (those would require IP22). It is classified as 'other ME equipment' requiring at least IP21; the device achieves IP22. The device is not intended to be used only while in a carrying case, so carrying-case-based IP provisions are N/A.

Clause 7.5.1 and 7.5.2: The device is not a permanently installed class I ME equipment, therefore all sub-clauses under 7.5.1 (protective earth installation warnings, earth conductor specifications, external protective earthing system verification) are N/A. The device does not require professional hygienic maintenance prior to re-use, therefore clause 7.5.2 is also N/A.
